newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Accused in U.N. Rwanda trial questions witness.
newsitem.headline: Accused in U.N. Rwanda trial questions witness.

text.p: In an unprecedented move, the U.N. Rwanda tribunal on Monday granted a request by an ethnic Hutu accused of genocide to directly cross-examine the first prosecution witness.

Presiding Judge Laity Kama said Jean-Paul Akayesu, the former mayor of Rwanda's Taba commune, was legally entitled to cross-examine a Tutsi accountant at the commune known to the court only as witness "K" to protect her identity.

"We will authorize the accused Jean-Paul Akayesu pursuant to Article 20 paragraph three to cross-examine the witness for the prosecution," Kama, of Senegal, said in response to Akayesu's request. Akayesu had also requested permission to dismiss his lawyers and a ruling is due later in the week.
Asked if she understood the court's decision, witness "K" replied: "No problem."
Akayesu started cross-examination in French from behind a screen flanked by two security guards while witness "K" wearing a brick-red suit replied in Kinyarwanda through an interpreter.
Cross-examination immediately led to heated exchanges and interruptions by Kama ordering clarifications from both Akayesu and the witness.
